text:
sophie: Hey @infra-oncall — onboarding a customer with Private VPC. Their onprem-installer fails during model pull + pip installs. Getting TLS failures and package fetch timeouts. Can we get an official egress allowlist and a quick validation checklist?

alex: can you paste the exact error output from the installer / agent? also what OS and network appliance (proxy/firewall) are they using?

sophie: Ubuntu 20.04, agent v1.4.2 package, customer behind a forward proxy + corporate firewall. Logs:
```
deploy-bot: installer: pulling model shard https://models.redwood.ai/shard/abc123
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
pip._internal.network.session: Retrying (Retry(total=2, connect=None, read=None, redirect=None)) after connection broken by 'SSLError("hostname 'files.pythonhosted.org' doesn't match 'pypi.org'")'
```

mike: two quick things to check: 1) make sure outbound 443 to our domains is allowed with SNI preserved (no TLS MITM that resigns certs), 2) allow OCSP/CRL hosts for certificate validation.

sophie: customer says TLS interception is allowed but they can add exceptions. They asked for a minimal host list and ports to request from their firewall team.

alex: minimal allowlist we typically send (HTTPS 443):
- registry.redwood.ai (model registry / shard pulls)
- models.redwood.ai (model artifacts CDN)
- storage.redwood.ai / s3.amazonaws.com (model shards + installer blobs)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (metrics/events)
- auth.redwood.ai (token exchange / keys)
- kms.redwood.ai (optional, if using Redwood KMS)
- files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.org (pip packages)
- deb.nodesource.com, packages.microsoft.com, repo.mongodb.org (common apt/yum sources customers may need)
- cdn.jsdelivr.net, cdn.pytorch.org (common wheel/cdn hosts)
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org, ocsp.globalsign.com, crl3.digicert.com (OCSP/CRL checks)

Also allow DNS (UDP 53/TCP 53) to their internal resolvers and/or allow upstream DNS to resolve those hosts. If TLS intercept is present, ensure SNI is passthrough for the Redwood domains or add TLS exception so the agent sees the original cert.

mike: add note about IP ranges — customers prefer hostnames. If they require IPs we can provide ranges but they change. Recommend FQDN allowlist with port 443.

sophie: repro checklist for them to validate after changes:
1) curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/health (should return 200 and correct cert chain)
2) python -c "import requests; requests.get('https://files.pythonhosted.org')"
3) sudo apt update (if apt hosts allowed)
4) run the onprem-installer with --verbose, confirm model shard downloads start and pip installs succeed

alex: Example troubleshooting commands to give firewall team: 
```
# TLS chain + SNI check
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai -showcerts
# curl with verbose to show cert issuer
curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/
```

deploy-bot: FYI installer records: attempt_id=fc3a2  stage=model_pull  error="x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"

infra-oncall: Thanks @sophie — can you confirm whether the customer wants us to provide a signed IP-range exception or they'll only accept FQDNs? If they want IPs we need a ticket to engineering to freeze artifact-hosting IPs for their firewall team.

sophie: they'll accept FQDNs but asked for a short IP fallback list for testing. I'll ask them to confirm and get back. For now sending this allowlist + commands. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex: Also tell them to check transparent proxy that re-signs certs: if present we need their proxy CA added to the host trust store or disable interception for the Redwoods hosts.

mike: adding quick note for support KB: include the above hosts + OCSP endpoints and the two openssl/curl checks. Keep entry minimal so customers can copy-paste to firewall team.

sophie: will do. Closing once customer confirms connectivity.
